requires_concepts: Gibbs measure of the SK model

outputs.exact_statement:
For every fixed $\beta>1$ and every fixed $a>0$, $$\mathbb P_{J,\,x_0\sim\pi^J}\{T^J(x_0)>n^a\}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_{J,\,x_0\sim\pi^J}
       \{T_{\mathrm{disc}}^J(x_0)>n^a\}\longrightarrow1.$$ Equivalently, each corresponding Gibbs mass tends to one in probability over the disorder.

Suppose an independent standard Gaussian vector $g$ at level $j$ enters the terminal exponent as $\sqrt v\,g\cdot e(S)$, where $e$ is a fixed vector-valued function of the terminal configuration. With all other parameters fixed, $$\label{static-eq:hierarchy-derivative}
 \frac{\partial}{\partial v}\mathbb EF_0
 =\frac12\left(
 \mathbb E\|e(S)\|^2-
 \sum_{l=j}^k w_l\mathbb E_l^{(2)}e(S^1)\cdot e(S^2)
 \right).$$ A quenched Gaussian is treated as level $0$. The identity holds for $v>0$ and extends to interpolation endpoints by integration and continuity.

For every fixed $\beta>0$, there is $C_\beta<\infty$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, $$\label{static-eq:finite-size}
 P_\beta-C_\beta n^{-1/24}\le p_n(\beta)\le P_\beta.$$

For every $0\le j\le k$, under the single-path law, $$\label{static-eq:field-energy-concentration}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}\left(\frac{z_j\cdot\sigma}{n}\right)\le\frac1n.$$

There exists $q_*\in(0,1)$, depending only on the fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$, with the following property. For each fixed $D_1>0$, there exists a fixed $D_3=D_3(\beta,D_1)>0$ and a sequence of events $\mathcal C_n(D_1)$, measurable with respect to the disorder, such that $\mathbb P_J(\mathcal C_n(D_1))\longrightarrow1$ and, on $\mathcal C_n(D_1)$, $$\pi^J\!\left(
   \left\{x\in S:
     \pi^J\{z\in S:|R(x,z)|\ge q_*\}<e^{-D_3L}
   \right\}\right)
 <e^{-D_1L}
 \qquad\text{for every }S\subset\{-1,1\}^n.
 \label{eq:coverage}$$

Fix $M>0$, $q\in(0,1)$, and $D\ge\beta^2M/2+2$. For all sufficiently large $n$, set $t=M\log n/n$. If $\nu$ is any deterministic probability measure on $\{-1,1\}^n$ satisfying $$\nu^{\otimes2}\{|R|\ge q\}\le4n^{-D},$$ and $G$ is standard Gaussian, define $W=\nu(e^{\beta\sqrt t H^G})$. There is a constant $C_\beta$, independent of $M,q,D,n,\nu$, such that $$\label{poly-eq:coverage-gain}
 \mathbb P_G\!\left(
 \log W\ge\frac{\beta^2t(n-1)}4
       -\beta^2ntq-C_\beta\sqrt{nt}-\log2
 \right)\ge\frac12.$$

With probability $1-o(1)$, for every $1\le j\le p$, every tuple $\boldsymbol v$ from banks $1,\ldots,j-1$, and every $0\le k\le m$, $$x_k\in S_j(\boldsymbol v)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{there is }\ell\le M_j\text{ such that }
 V_{j,\ell}\in S_j(\boldsymbol v),\quad
 |R(V_{j,\ell},x_k)|\ge q_*.$$ This event depends only on $J$, the chain and the bank lists, and is independent of the thresholds.

With probability $1-o(1)$, for every $i<j\le p$, every entry $v$ of bank $i$, every entry $w$ of bank $j$, and every $0\le k\le m$, $$\label{fixed-eq:all-bank-locking}
 \begin{gathered}
 |R(x_k,w)|\ge t_j/2,\qquad
 |R(v,x_k)|,\ |R(v,w)|\le b_j
 \\
 \Longrightarrow\qquad
 \bigl||R(v,x_k)|-|R(v,w)|\bigr|\le2\delta_n.
 \end{gathered}$$

For all sufficiently large $n$, on $\mathcal G_n\cap\mathcal S_n$ every reference selection and every crossing succeeds. For every $1\le j\le p$, $$\label{fixed-eq:nested-shells}
 |D_{v_j}(\tau_j)-r_j|\le2/n,\qquad
 |D_{v_i}(\tau_j)-r_i|\le6j\delta_n
                  \quad(1\le i\le j).$$
